The coupled cam ring advances all jaw carriages until the pivoting pads seat on the pipe. content.content:
1	Equipment is frequently attached to the outside of a pipe after the pipe has been installed. Sensors, small tools, brackets, and lengths of conduit all have to be carried on a pipe that cannot be taken out of service, cannot be lifted, and has no free end over which a closed ring could be threaded. A clamp intended for that duty therefore has to open from the side, close around the pipe, and grip it firmly enough that the carried equipment keeps its position, while remaining removable so that the same clamp can be taken off and used again elsewhere.
2	
3	A clamp that opens from the side is split into parts, and the split is what makes the gripping problem difficult. Once the clamp body is divided, any drive element that runs around the body is divided with it. If the gripping surfaces of each part are driven separately, the fixed relationship between the two parts of the drive is given up: the two sides of the clamp advance by amounts that depend on how each side is operated, so the clamp tends to settle off center on the pipe, and the load is shared unevenly between the gripping surfaces. If the split body is instead pulled closed on the pipe, the closing force passes through the joint at the split and the pipe itself reacts the closing motion, so the grip depends on how nearly the bore of the clamp matches the outside diameter of the pipe, and a part dimensioned to a particular pipe diameter is needed, so that a different pipe size calls for a different part.
4	
5	Reusable clamping also has to deal with the force the operator applies. A hand lever gives the operator no measure of what has been done to the pipe. When the gripping elements have reached the pipe, further travel of the lever has to go somewhere, and in a rigid drive train it goes into whichever gripping element happens to touch first, so that one gripping surface is loaded far more than the others. Concentrated loading of a single gripping surface is undesirable, and the operator has no indication that it has occurred. An added instrument that responds to the position of the gripping elements reports the size of the pipe rather than the force in the grip.
6	
7	What has been lacking is a split clamp in which the drive that advances the gripping elements is itself coupled by the act of closing the clamp into a single element that moves as one ring, in which every gripping element is advanced from that one drive so that the gripping elements advance together over a range of pipe sizes, and in which the travel remaining in the operator's lever after the gripping elements have landed on the pipe is absorbed within the clamp and reported to the operator as a loading condition rather than as a dimension.
8

3	In one aspect, a split pipe clamp comprises a first frame half and a second frame half joined at a hinge end by a hinge and releasably joined at a latch end by a latch. In a closed condition the two frame halves define a frame having an annular guide and three radial guides. Three jaw carriages are each slidable radially in a respective one of the radial guides, and each jaw carriage carries a jaw pad that is pivotally mounted on the jaw carriage and has a concave bearing face directed inwardly of the frame. A wedge movable by the latch bears on a ring drive face of the segmented cam ring, so that movement of the latch rotates the coupled ring through the stroke, and a carriage return spring biases each jaw carriage outwardly so that releasing the latch retracts the jaws.

1	The following description of embodiments refers to the accompanying drawings. The same reference numeral denotes the same part throughout. Terms of direction are used with respect to the frame of the clamp: the axis of the frame is the axis about which the frame is annular in the closed condition, "inward" and "radially inward" mean toward that axis, "outward" and "radially outward" mean away from it, and "circumferential" means about that axis. These terms describe relationships within the clamp and do not require the clamp to be used in any particular attitude.
2	
3	Overall arrangement
4	
5	FIG. 1 shows a split pipe clamp 100 closed around a pipe 90, with the latch 16 in the over-center position described below and the jaw pads 40 seated on the pipe 90. The clamp 100 has a first frame half 10 and a second frame half 12. Each of the first frame half 10 and the second frame half 12 is semicircular, and the two frame halves together surround the pipe 90. The first frame half 10 and the second frame half 12 are joined at one end, referred to as the hinge end, by a hinge 14, and are releasably joined at the other end, referred to as the latch end, by a releasable latch 16. The hinge 14 permits the first frame half 10 and the second frame half 12 to be swung apart far enough for the frame halves to be placed around the pipe 90 from the side. When the frame halves are brought together and the latch 16 is engaged, the first frame half 10 and the second frame half 12 define a frame that is annular about the axis of the frame.
6	
7	Three jaw carriages 30 are distributed around the frame in the closed condition, so that the three jaw carriages 30 approach the pipe 90 from three different directions. Each jaw carriage 30 moves radially with respect to the frame and carries at its inner end a jaw pad 40, which is described below in connection with FIG. 3. The jaw pads 40 carried at the inner ends of the three jaw carriages 30 bear on the pipe 90 when the clamp 100 is clamped. The clamp 100 does not require a part dimensioned to a particular pipe diameter, and the same clamp 100 serves pipes of different diameters within the radial travel of the jaw carriages 30.
8	
9	The frame may carry a mounting boss 70 outside the annular guide 18 described below, as shown in FIG. 5, which is a fragmentary view with parts shown in section on a plane containing the axis of the frame and corresponding in orientation to the plane of FIG. 3, that plane passing through the mounting boss 70. The mounting boss 70 supports equipment 80 that is to be held on the pipe 90 by the clamp 100. FIG. 5 shows the equipment 80 supported on the mounting boss 70, the equipment 80 being a sensor, a tool, or a conduit. The mounting boss 70 does not participate in the advance of the three jaw carriages 30 inwardly in synchronism. FIG. 5 also shows the annular guide 18 of the frame with the segmented cam ring 20 received in it, the mounting boss 70 standing outside the annular guide 18, no part of the mounting boss 70 reaching into the annular guide 18. The equipment 80 carried at the mounting boss 70 therefore lies outside the drive path by which the jaws are advanced. The mounting boss 70 is an optional feature of the clamp 100 and may be omitted.
10	
11	The segmented cam ring
12	
13	FIG. 2 shows the segmented cam ring 20, drawn removed from the frame, its segments being in the relative positions they occupy when coupled in the closed condition. The segmented cam ring 20 comprises a first cam ring segment 22 and a second cam ring segment 24. The first cam ring segment 22 is carried by the first frame half 10 and the second cam ring segment 24 is carried by the second frame half 12, so that each frame half carries one segment of the ring and each segment travels with its own frame half when the clamp 100 is opened.
14	
15	The first cam ring segment 22 and the second cam ring segment 24 meet at two places, one at the hinge end and one at the latch end. At the hinge end the two segments have complementary coupling faces 26, and at the latch end they have complementary coupling faces 28. The complementary coupling faces 26 and the complementary coupling faces 28 are each shaped so that one segment can transmit circumferential force to the other through the joint. The faces are brought into engagement by the same motion that closes the frame halves: as the first frame half 10 and the second frame half 12 are swung together about the hinge 14, the complementary coupling faces 26 close on one another at the hinge end and the complementary coupling faces 28 close on one another at the latch end. FIG. 6 shows the joint at the latch end in the closed condition, the end of the first cam ring segment 22 held by the first frame half 10 and the end of the second cam ring segment 24 held by the second frame half 12, the two ends meeting at the complementary coupling faces 28.
16	
17	Coupling the segments in this way solves a problem created by splitting the clamp. Here the division of the ring is undone by the act of closing the clamp. In the closed condition the first cam ring segment 22 and the second cam ring segment 24 are coupled at both ends and rotate together in the annular guide as a coupled ring, and a circumferential input applied to either segment is carried around the whole ring. One input, applied at one point on one frame half, therefore reaches every jaw carriage 30 through a single kinematic element, and the relationship between the jaw carriages 30 is set by the geometry of the ring rather than by the way the clamp is operated. When the latch 16 is released and the frame halves are swung apart, the complementary coupling faces 26 and the complementary coupling faces 28 separate and each segment stays with its own frame half, so that the coupling is made and broken by the closing and opening of the frame halves.
18	
19	The annular guide 18 retains the first cam ring segment 22 on the first frame half 10 and the second cam ring segment 24 on the second frame half 12, and permits circumferential movement of the coupled ring. Each segment is therefore held on its own frame half whether the clamp 100 is open or closed, and no separate operation is needed to place the ring in the frame when the frame halves are brought together.
20	
21	The segmented cam ring 20 has three oblique slots 34, one for each jaw carriage 30. Each oblique slot 34 is inclined to the radial direction of the frame at the circumferential position of that slot, so that rotation of the coupled ring produces inward travel of its jaw carriage 30, the three oblique slots 34 being arranged so that the three jaw carriages 30 travel inwardly in synchronism.
22	
23	The segmented cam ring 20 further has a ring drive face 36, shown in FIG. 2 at the latch end of the ring, against which the latch 16 acts through a wedge 52 as described below. The ring drive face 36 is presented at a position on the ring that the wedge 52 can reach, so that advance of the wedge 52 against the ring drive face 36 moves the segmented cam ring 20 circumferentially.
24	
25	The jaw carriages
26	
27	FIG. 3 is a fragmentary sectional view through one jaw carriage 30, taken on line 3-3 of FIG. 1. The frame is formed with the annular guide 18, which receives the segmented cam ring 20 and holds it against radial movement while leaving it free to move circumferentially.
28

The radial guide 38 prevents the jaw carriage 30, and therefore the follower 32, from moving circumferentially, while the oblique slot 34 holds the follower 32 at a position along the slot, which is inclined to the radial direction, so that circumferential movement of the segmented cam ring 20 displaces the follower 32 radially. When the coupled ring turns through its stroke, the side of each oblique slot 34 bears on the corresponding follower 32 and drives it, and with it the jaw carriage 30, radially inward along the radial guide 38. If the drive train from the latch handle 50 to the wedge 52 were rigid, that remaining travel would be taken up by whatever part of the assembly yielded first, in practice by driving one jaw farther into the pipe 90 than the others and loading it far more heavily. The following description of embodiments refers to the accompanying drawings. The same reference numeral denotes the same part throughout. Terms of direction are used with respect to the frame of the clamp: the axis of the frame is the axis about which the frame is annular in the closed condition, "inward" and "radially inward" mean toward that axis, "outward" and "radially outward" mean away from it, and "circumferential" means about that axis. These terms describe relationships within the clamp and do not require the clamp to be used in any particular attitude.

Overall arrangement

FIG. 1 shows a split pipe clamp 100 closed around a pipe 90, with the latch 16 in the over-center position described below and the jaw pads 40 seated on the pipe 90. The clamp 100 has a first frame half 10 and a second frame half 12. Each of the first frame half 10 and the second frame half 12 is semicircular, and the two frame halves together surround the pipe 90. The first frame half 10 and the second frame half 12 are joined at one end, referred to as the hinge end, by a hinge 14, and are releasably joined at the other end, referred to as the latch end, by a releasable latch 16. The hinge 14 permits the first frame half 10 and the second frame half 12 to be swung apart far enough for the frame halves to be placed around the pipe 90 from the side. When the frame halves are brought together and the latch 16 is engaged, the first frame half 10 and the second frame half 12 define a frame that is annular about the axis of the frame.

Three jaw carriages 30 are distributed around the frame in the closed condition, so that the three jaw carriages 30 approach the pipe 90 from three different directions. Each jaw carriage 30 moves radially with respect to the frame and carries at its inner end a jaw pad 40, which is described below in connection with FIG. 3. The jaw pads 40 carried at the inner ends of the three jaw carriages 30 bear on the pipe 90 when the clamp 100 is clamped. The clamp 100 does not require a part dimensioned to a particular pipe diameter, and the same clamp 100 serves pipes of different diameters within the radial travel of the jaw carriages 30.

The frame may carry a mounting boss 70 outside the annular guide 18 described below, as shown in FIG. 5, which is a fragmentary view with parts shown in section on a plane containing the axis of the frame and corresponding in orientation to the plane of FIG. 3, that plane passing through the mounting boss 70. The mounting boss 70 supports equipment 80 that is to be held on the pipe 90 by the clamp 100. FIG. 5 shows the equipment 80 supported on the mounting boss 70, the equipment 80 being a sensor, a tool, or a conduit. The mounting boss 70 does not participate in the advance of the three jaw carriages 30 inwardly in synchronism. FIG. 5 also shows the annular guide 18 of the frame with the segmented cam ring 20 received in it, the mounting boss 70 standing outside the annular guide 18, no part of the mounting boss 70 reaching into the annular guide 18. The equipment 80 carried at the mounting boss 70 therefore lies outside the drive path by which the jaws are advanced. The mounting boss 70 is an optional feature of the clamp 100 and may be omitted.

The segmented cam ring

FIG. 2 shows the segmented cam ring 20, drawn removed from the frame, its segments being in the relative positions they occupy when coupled in the closed condition. The segmented cam ring 20 comprises a first cam ring segment 22 and a second cam ring segment 24. The first cam ring segment 22 is carried by the first frame half 10 and the second cam ring segment 24 is carried by the second frame half 12, so that each frame half carries one segment of the ring and each segment travels with its own frame half when the clamp 100 is opened.

The first cam ring segment 22 and the second cam ring segment 24 meet at two places, one at the hinge end and one at the latch end. At the hinge end the two segments have complementary coupling faces 26, and at the latch end they have complementary coupling faces 28. The complementary coupling faces 26 and the complementary coupling faces 28 are each shaped so that one segment can transmit circumferential force to the other through the joint. The faces are brought into engagement by the same motion that closes the frame halves: as the first frame half 10 and the second frame half 12 are swung together about the hinge 14, the complementary coupling faces 26 close on one another at the hinge end and the complementary coupling faces 28 close on one another at the latch end. FIG. 6 shows the joint at the latch end in the closed condition, the end of the first cam ring segment 22 held by the first frame half 10 and the end of the second cam ring segment 24 held by the second frame half 12, the two ends meeting at the complementary coupling faces 28.

Coupling the segments in this way solves a problem created by splitting the clamp. Here the division of the ring is undone by the act of closing the clamp. In the closed condition the first cam ring segment 22 and the second cam ring segment 24 are coupled at both ends and rotate together in the annular guide as a coupled ring, and a circumferential input applied to either segment is carried around the whole ring. One input, applied at one point on one frame half, therefore reaches every jaw carriage 30 through a single kinematic element, and the relationship between the jaw carriages 30 is set by the geometry of the ring rather than by the way the clamp is operated. When the latch 16 is released and the frame halves are swung apart, the complementary coupling faces 26 and the complementary coupling faces 28 separate and each segment stays with its own frame half, so that the coupling is made and broken by the closing and opening of the frame halves.

The annular guide 18 retains the first cam ring segment 22 on the first frame half 10 and the second cam ring segment 24 on the second frame half 12, and permits circumferential movement of the coupled ring. Each segment is therefore held on its own frame half whether the clamp 100 is open or closed, and no separate operation is needed to place the ring in the frame when the frame halves are brought together.

The segmented cam ring 20 has three oblique slots 34, one for each jaw carriage 30. Each oblique slot 34 is inclined to the radial direction of the frame at the circumferential position of that slot, so that rotation of the coupled ring produces inward travel of its jaw carriage 30, the three oblique slots 34 being arranged so that the three jaw carriages 30 travel inwardly in synchronism.

The segmented cam ring 20 further has a ring drive face 36, shown in FIG. 2 at the latch end of the ring, against which the latch 16 acts through a wedge 52 as described below. The ring drive face 36 is presented at a position on the ring that the wedge 52 can reach, so that advance of the wedge 52 against the ring drive face 36 moves the segmented cam ring 20 circumferentially.

The jaw carriages

FIG. 3 is a fragmentary sectional view through one jaw carriage 30, taken on line 3-3 of FIG. 1. The frame is formed with the annular guide 18, which receives the segmented cam ring 20 and holds it against radial movement while leaving it free to move circumferentially.

The frame is further formed with a radial guide 38 at the position of each jaw carriage 30, so that the frame in the closed condition has the annular guide 18 and three radial guides 38. Each jaw carriage 30 is received in a respective one of the three radial guides 38 and is constrained by the radial guide 38 to move radially with respect to the frame. Each jaw carriage 30 carries a follower 32 that projects from the jaw carriage 30 into a respective one of the oblique slots 34 of the segmented cam ring 20. The follower 32 bears against the sides of the oblique slot 34.

The follower 32 is constrained in two ways at once. The radial guide 38 prevents the jaw carriage 30, and therefore the follower 32, from moving circumferentially, while the oblique slot 34 holds the follower 32 at a position along the slot, which is inclined to the radial direction, so that circumferential movement of the segmented cam ring 20 displaces the follower 32 radially. When the coupled ring turns through its stroke, the side of each oblique slot 34 bears on the corresponding follower 32 and drives it, and with it the jaw carriage 30, radially inward along the radial guide 38. Because all three followers 32 are engaged in oblique slots 34 of one coupled ring, the three jaw carriages 30 advance inwardly in synchronism for as long as the ring turns. The jaw pads 40 therefore close on the pipe together.

At its inner end each jaw carriage 30 carries a jaw pad 40. The jaw pad 40 is pivotally mounted on the jaw carriage 30 and has a concave bearing face directed inwardly of the frame. Because the jaw pad 40 is free to pivot on the jaw carriage 30, the concave bearing face aligns itself with the outer surface of the pipe as it lands. The same concave bearing face therefore seats on pipes of different diameters, and no part dimensioned to a particular pipe diameter is required.

A carriage return spring 44 acts on each jaw carriage 30 so as to urge that jaw carriage 30 radially outward. When the latch 16 is released and the drive from the latch to the ring drive face 36 is removed, the carriage return springs 44 push the jaw carriages 30 outward and the jaw pads 40 are retracted from the pipe, and the clamp 100 is left with its jaw carriages 30 retracted and ready for the next installation. Retraction of the jaw carriages 30 clears the jaw pads 40 from the pipe before the frame halves are swung apart.

The latch and the force-limiting drive train

The latch 16 comprises a latch housing 58 at the latch end, a latch handle 50, and a force-limiting spring stack 54 in a drive train between the latch handle 50 and the wedge 52, the wedge 52 being movable by the latch 16. The latch housing 58 presents a fixed edge referred to below in connection with the indicator pin 56. The wedge 52 is positioned to bear on the ring drive face 36 of the segmented cam ring 20.

FIG. 4 is an enlarged fragmentary view of the latch end, with parts shown in section, and shows the latch housing 58, the latch handle 50, the wedge 52, the force-limiting spring stack 54 and the indicator pin 56 in their relation to the first cam ring segment 22, the second cam ring segment 24 and the ring drive face 36.

The latch 16 has two engaged positions. In a first position, the latch 16 holds the first frame half 10 and the second frame half 12 closed around the pipe 90 but does not clamp it: the frame is captive on the pipe 90 and cannot fall away, while the segmented cam ring 20 has not yet advanced the jaw carriages 30. In a second, over-center position, the wedge 52 drives the segmented cam ring 20 and the pipe 90 is clamped. Movement of the latch handle 50 from the first position to the second position advances the wedge 52 against the ring drive face 36. That advance moves the segmented cam ring 20 circumferentially, and the coupled ring turns through its limited stroke.

The force-limiting spring stack 54 answers the problem of what becomes of the operator's remaining handle travel. The jaw pads 40 land on the pipe 90 at some point in the stroke that depends on the diameter of the pipe 90, and the latch handle 50 has still to be carried into its over-center position. If the drive train from the latch handle 50 to the wedge 52 were rigid, that remaining travel would be taken up by whatever part of the assembly yielded first, in practice by driving one jaw farther into the pipe 90 than the others and loading it far more heavily. Additional travel of the latch handle 50 after all three jaw pads 40 have contacted the pipe 90 compresses the force-limiting spring stack 54 rather than forcing one jaw carriage 30 farther inward than the others.

The indicator pin 56 is coupled to the force-limiting spring stack 54 and projects from the latch housing 58. As the force-limiting spring stack 54 compresses, the indicator pin 56 moves relative to a fixed edge of the latch housing 58, and the position of the indicator pin 56 with respect to that fixed edge shows the operator when the force-limiting spring stack 54 has entered a predetermined compression range. The indicator pin 56 therefore reports clamp loading mechanically, and what it reports is the state of the force-limiting spring stack 54. The indicator pin 56 is displaced by compression of the force-limiting spring stack 54 independently of a diameter of the pipe 90, and its position is not a measurement of that diameter.

Operation

To install the clamp 100 on a pipe 90, the operator opens the latch 16 and swings the first frame half 10 and the second frame half 12 apart about the hinge 14. The first cam ring segment 22 stays with the first frame half 10 and the second cam ring segment 24 stays with the second frame half 12, and the complementary coupling faces 26 and the complementary coupling faces 28 are separated. The operator places the frame halves around the pipe 90 from the side and closes them about the hinge 14. Closing the frame halves brings the complementary coupling faces 26 into engagement at the hinge end and the complementary coupling faces 28 into engagement at the latch end, coupling the first cam ring segment 22 and the second cam ring segment 24 into the coupled ring within the annular guide 18.

The operator then moves the latch 16 to its first position, in which the frame is held around the pipe 90 without clamping. The operator moves the latch handle 50 to the second, over-center position. The wedge 52 is driven against the ring drive face 36, the coupled ring turns through its stroke, the sides of the three oblique slots 34 drive the three followers 32, and the three jaw carriages 30 advance inwardly in synchronism until the pivoting jaw pads 40 seat on the pipe 90. The remaining travel of the latch handle 50 compresses the force-limiting spring stack 54, and the operator watches the indicator pin 56 move relative to the fixed edge of the latch housing 58 and so sees that the force-limiting spring stack 54 has entered the predetermined compression range. The latch 16 is left in the over-center position and the clamp 100 is loaded on the pipe 90.

To remove the clamp 100, the operator releases the latch 16. The latch handle 50 comes back over center, the wedge 52 retreats from the ring drive face 36, and the force-limiting spring stack 54 is unloaded. The carriage return springs 44 then push the jaw carriages 30 radially outward, so that the jaw pads 40 lift from the pipe 90. Only then are the first frame half 10 and the second frame half 12 swung apart about the hinge 14 and the clamp 100 taken off the pipe 90. The clamp 100 may be installed again on the same pipe or on a pipe of a different diameter within the radial travel of the jaw carriages 30.

Features described above in connection with one embodiment may be combined with features described in connection with another, except where the context makes the combination impossible. The embodiments described are illustrative of the disclosed clamp and are not exhaustive of it, and the scope of protection is defined by the claims that follow rather than by any particular embodiment described here.

Plan view of the split pipe clamp closed around a pipe, viewed along the pipe axis. Black line work on white, well inside the drawing area.

The pipe 90 is seen end on at the centre of the drawing area as a circle with its interior blank. An annular frame body surrounds it, bounded by an inner circle spaced outward from the pipe 90 and by an outer circle. The ring-shaped space between the pipe 90 and that inner circle is open, crossed only by the jaw pads 40 and the inner ends of the jaw carriages 30.

Two radial joint lines, at the left and at the right, divide the annular frame body into two semicircular bodies: the upper is the first frame half 10, the lower the second frame half 12.

At the left joint is the hinge 14, shown schematically as a small circle on that joint line between the inner circle and the outer circle.

At the right joint is the latch 16, shown schematically as a rectangular block outside the frame body bridging both frame ends, with a lever reaching radially outward from it, the lever's attitude shown schematically, drawn inclined toward the first frame half 10 to represent the latch in the over-center position.

At each position the inner circle is interrupted by a radial opening and the jaw carriage 30 is shown schematically as a block reaching radially inward through that opening, its outer portion within the body and its inner end inside the inner circle.

Each jaw carriage 30 carries at its inner end a separate member, the jaw pad 40, joined at a small circle, a pivot shown schematically; its inner face is a concave arc meeting the pipe 90.

A short broken cutting-plane line lies in the upper part of the view on the radial centre line of the topmost jaw carriage 30, its outer end just outside the outer circle and its inner end at the pipe 90. 5	A reusable split pipe clamp has a first semicircular frame half and a second semicircular frame half joined by a hinge at one end and a releasable latch at the other end. Each carriage slides in a radial guide and carries a pivoting concave jaw pad that bears on a pipe without requiring a tool-specific pipe diameter.
6	
7	A segmented cam ring is retained in an annular guide of the frame. One cam-ring segment is carried by each frame half. When the halves close, complementary drive faces at the hinge and latch ends couple the segments so that they move as one ring. Each jaw carriage has a follower received in a respective oblique slot of the cam ring. Closing the latch drives a wedge against a drive face of the cam ring and rotates the coupled ring through a limited stroke. The oblique slots translate that rotation into synchronized inward travel of all three jaw carriages. A spring biases each carriage outward when the latch is released.
8	
9	The latch has a first position that holds the frame halves around the pipe without clamping and a second over-center position that drives the cam ring and clamps the pipe. A force-limiting spring stack lies between the latch handle and the wedge, so additional handle travel after all jaw pads contact the pipe compresses the spring stack rather than forcing one jaw farther than the others. A visible indicator pin moves relative to a fixed edge of the latch housing when the spring stack enters a predetermined compression range. The indicator reports clamp loading mechanically and does not measure pipe diameter.
10	
11	To install the clamp, an operator opens the latch, swings the frame halves apart, places them around a pipe, closes the frame, moves the latch to the holding position, and then moves the latch to the over-center position. The coupled cam ring advances all jaw carriages until the pivoting pads seat on the pipe. To remove the clamp, releasing the latch unloads the spring stack and the carriage springs retract the jaws before the frame halves are opened.
12	
13	The frame may carry a mounting boss outside the annular guide for supporting a sensor, tool, or conduit. The mounting boss does not participate in jaw synchronization. The disclosed essential relationship is that closure couples the ring segments and latch travel drives the coupled ring, while the oblique slots synchronize the radial jaw carriages and the force-limiting spring stack accommodates the remaining latch travel.

Each carriage slides in a radial guide and carries a pivoting concave jaw pad that bears on a pipe without requiring a tool-specific pipe diameter.

A segmented cam ring is retained in an annular guide of the frame. One cam-ring segment is carried by each frame half. When the halves close, complementary drive faces at the hinge and latch ends couple the segments so that they move as one ring. Each jaw carriage has a follower received in a respective oblique slot of the cam ring. Closing the latch drives a wedge against a drive face of the cam ring and rotates the coupled ring through a limited stroke. A force-limiting spring stack lies between the latch handle and the wedge, so additional handle travel after all jaw pads contact the pipe compresses the spring stack rather than forcing one jaw farther than the others. A visible indicator pin moves relative to a fixed edge of the latch housing when the spring stack enters a predetermined compression range. The coupled cam ring advances all jaw carriages until the pivoting pads seat on the pipe. To remove the clamp, releasing the latch unloads the spring stack and the carriage springs retract the jaws before the frame halves are opened.

The frame may carry a mounting boss outside the annular guide for supporting a sensor, tool, or conduit. The mounting boss does not participate in jaw synchronization. The disclosed essential relationship is that closure couples the ring segments and latch travel drives the coupled ring, while the oblique slots synchronize the radial jaw carriages and the force-limiting spring stack accommodates the remaining latch travel.

1	Equipment is frequently attached to the outside of a pipe after the pipe has been installed. Sensors, small tools, brackets, and lengths of conduit all have to be carried on a pipe that cannot be taken out of service, cannot be lifted, and has no free end over which a closed ring could be threaded. A clamp intended for that duty therefore has to open from the side, close around the pipe, and grip it firmly enough that the carried equipment keeps its position, while remaining removable so that the same clamp can be taken off and used again elsewhere.
2	
3	A clamp that opens from the side is split into parts, and the split is what makes the gripping problem difficult. Once the clamp body is divided, any drive element that runs around the body is divided with it. If the gripping surfaces of each part are driven separately, the fixed relationship between the two parts of the drive is given up: the two sides of the clamp advance by amounts that depend on how each side is operated, so the clamp tends to settle off center on the pipe, and the load is shared unevenly between the gripping surfaces. If the split body is instead pulled closed on the pipe, the closing force passes through the joint at the split and the pipe itself reacts the closing motion, so the grip depends on how nearly the bore of the clamp matches the outside diameter of the pipe, and a part dimensioned to a particular pipe diameter is needed, so that a different pipe size calls for a different part.
4	
5	Reusable clamping also has to deal with the force the operator applies. A hand lever gives the operator no measure of what has been done to the pipe. When the gripping elements have reached the pipe, further travel of the lever has to go somewhere, and in a rigid drive train it goes into whichever gripping element happens to touch first, so that one gripping surface is loaded far more than the others. Concentrated loading of a single gripping surface is undesirable, and the operator has no indication that it has occurred. An added instrument that responds to the position of the gripping elements reports the size of the pipe rather than the force in the grip.
6	
7	What has been lacking is a split clamp in which the drive that advances the gripping elements is itself coupled by the act of closing the clamp into a single element that moves as one ring, in which every gripping element is advanced from that one drive so that the gripping elements advance together over a range of pipe sizes, and in which the travel remaining in the operator's lever after the gripping elements have landed on the pipe is absorbed within the clamp and reported to the operator as a loading condition rather than as a dimension.
8

1	The following description of embodiments refers to the accompanying drawings. The same reference numeral denotes the same part throughout. Terms of direction are used with respect to the frame of the clamp: the axis of the frame is the axis about which the frame is annular in the closed condition, "inward" and "radially inward" mean toward that axis, "outward" and "radially outward" mean away from it, and "circumferential" means about that axis. These terms describe relationships within the clamp and do not require the clamp to be used in any particular attitude.
2	
3	Overall arrangement
4	
5	FIG. 1 shows a split pipe clamp 100 closed around a pipe 90, with the latch 16 in the over-center position described below and the jaw pads 40 seated on the pipe 90. The clamp 100 has a first frame half 10 and a second frame half 12. Each of the first frame half 10 and the second frame half 12 is semicircular, and the two frame halves together surround the pipe 90. The first frame half 10 and the second frame half 12 are joined at one end, referred to as the hinge end, by a hinge 14, and are releasably joined at the other end, referred to as the latch end, by a releasable latch 16. The hinge 14 permits the first frame half 10 and the second frame half 12 to be swung apart far enough for the frame halves to be placed around the pipe 90 from the side. When the frame halves are brought together and the latch 16 is engaged, the first frame half 10 and the second frame half 12 define a frame that is annular about the axis of the frame.
6	
7	Three jaw carriages 30 are distributed around the frame in the closed condition, so that the three jaw carriages 30 approach the pipe 90 from three different directions. Each jaw carriage 30 moves radially with respect to the frame and carries at its inner end a jaw pad 40, which is described below in connection with FIG. 3. The jaw pads 40 carried at the inner ends of the three jaw carriages 30 bear on the pipe 90 when the clamp 100 is clamped. The clamp 100 does not require a part dimensioned to a particular pipe diameter, and the same clamp 100 serves pipes of different diameters within the radial travel of the jaw carriages 30.
8	
9	The frame may carry a mounting boss 70 outside the annular guide 18 described below, as shown in FIG. 5, which is a fragmentary view with parts shown in section on a plane containing the axis of the frame and corresponding in orientation to the plane of FIG. 3, that plane passing through the mounting boss 70. The mounting boss 70 supports equipment 80 that is to be held on the pipe 90 by the clamp 100. FIG. 5 shows the equipment 80 supported on the mounting boss 70, the equipment 80 being a sensor, a tool, or a conduit. The mounting boss 70 does not participate in the advance of the three jaw carriages 30 inwardly in synchronism. FIG. 5 also shows the annular guide 18 of the frame with the segmented cam ring 20 received in it, the mounting boss 70 standing outside the annular guide 18, no part of the mounting boss 70 reaching into the annular guide 18. The equipment 80 carried at the mounting boss 70 therefore lies outside the drive path by which the jaws are advanced. The mounting boss 70 is an optional feature of the clamp 100 and may be omitted.
10	
11	The segmented cam ring
12	
13	FIG. 2 shows the segmented cam ring 20, drawn removed from the frame, its segments being in the relative positions they occupy when coupled in the closed condition. The segmented cam ring 20 comprises a first cam ring segment 22 and a second cam ring segment 24. The first cam ring segment 22 is carried by the first frame half 10 and the second cam ring segment 24 is carried by the second frame half 12, so that each frame half carries one segment of the ring and each segment travels with its own frame half when the clamp 100 is opened.
14	
15	The first cam ring segment 22 and the second cam ring segment 24 meet at two places, one at the hinge end and one at the latch end. At the hinge end the two segments have complementary coupling faces 26, and at the latch end they have complementary coupling faces 28. The complementary coupling faces 26 and the complementary coupling faces 28 are each shaped so that one segment can transmit circumferential force to the other through the joint. The faces are brought into engagement by the same motion that closes the frame halves: as the first frame half 10 and the second frame half 12 are swung together about the hinge 14, the complementary coupling faces 26 close on one another at the hinge end and the complementary coupling faces 28 close on one another at the latch end. FIG. 6 shows the joint at the latch end in the closed condition, the end of the first cam ring segment 22 held by the first frame half 10 and the end of the second cam ring segment 24 held by the second frame half 12, the two ends meeting at the complementary coupling faces 28.
16	
17	Coupling the segments in this way solves a problem created by splitting the clamp. Here the division of the ring is undone by the act of closing the clamp. In the closed condition the first cam ring segment 22 and the second cam ring segment 24 are coupled at both ends and rotate together in the annular guide as a coupled ring, and a circumferential input applied to either segment is carried around the whole ring. One input, applied at one point on one frame half, therefore reaches every jaw carriage 30 through a single kinematic element, and the relationship between the jaw carriages 30 is set by the geometry of the ring rather than by the way the clamp is operated. When the latch 16 is released and the frame halves are swung apart, the complementary coupling faces 26 and the complementary coupling faces 28 separate and each segment stays with its own frame half, so that the coupling is made and broken by the closing and opening of the frame halves.
18	
19	The annular guide 18 retains the first cam ring segment 22 on the first frame half 10 and the second cam ring segment 24 on the second frame half 12, and permits circumferential movement of the coupled ring. Each segment is therefore held on its own frame half whether the clamp 100 is open or closed, and no separate operation is needed to place the ring in the frame when the frame halves are brought together.
20	
21	The segmented cam ring 20 has three oblique slots 34, one for each jaw carriage 30. Each oblique slot 34 is inclined to the radial direction of the frame at the circumferential position of that slot, so that rotation of the coupled ring produces inward travel of its jaw carriage 30, the three oblique slots 34 being arranged so that the three jaw carriages 30 travel inwardly in synchronism.
22	
23	The segmented cam ring 20 further has a ring drive face 36, shown in FIG. 2 at the latch end of the ring, against which the latch 16 acts through a wedge 52 as described below. The ring drive face 36 is presented at a position on the ring that the wedge 52 can reach, so that advance of the wedge 52 against the ring drive face 36 moves the segmented cam ring 20 circumferentially.
24	
25	The jaw carriages
26	
27	FIG. 3 is a fragmentary sectional view through one jaw carriage 30, taken on line 3-3 of FIG. 1. The frame is formed with the annular guide 18, which receives the segmented cam ring 20 and holds it against radial movement while leaving it free to move circumferentially.
28	
29	The frame is further formed with a radial guide 38 at the position of each jaw carriage 30, so that the frame in the closed condition has the annular guide 18 and three radial guides 38. Each jaw carriage 30 is received in a respective one of the three radial guides 38 and is constrained by the radial guide 38 to move radially with respect to the frame. Each jaw carriage 30 carries a follower 32 that projects from the jaw carriage 30 into a respective one of the oblique slots 34 of the segmented cam ring 20. The follower 32 bears against the sides of the oblique slot 34.
30	
31	The follower 32 is constrained in two ways at once. The radial guide 38 prevents the jaw carriage 30, and therefore the follower 32, from moving circumferentially, while the oblique slot 34 holds the follower 32 at a position along the slot, which is inclined to the radial direction, so that circumferential movement of the segmented cam ring 20 displaces the follower 32 radially. When the coupled ring turns through its stroke, the side of each oblique slot 34 bears on the corresponding follower 32 and drives it, and with it the jaw carriage 30, radially inward along the radial guide 38. Because all three followers 32 are engaged in oblique slots 34 of one coupled ring, the three jaw carriages 30 advance inwardly in synchronism for as long as the ring turns. The jaw pads 40 therefore close on the pipe together.
32	
33	At its inner end each jaw carriage 30 carries a jaw pad 40. The jaw pad 40 is pivotally mounted on the jaw carriage 30 and has a concave bearing face directed inwardly of the frame. Because the jaw pad 40 is free to pivot on the jaw carriage 30, the concave bearing face aligns itself with the outer surface of the pipe as it lands. The same concave bearing face therefore seats on pipes of different diameters, and no part dimensioned to a particular pipe diameter is required.
34	
35	A carriage return spring 44 acts on each jaw carriage 30 so as to urge that jaw carriage 30 radially outward. When the latch 16 is released and the drive from the latch to the ring drive face 36 is removed, the carriage return springs 44 push the jaw carriages 30 outward and the jaw pads 40 are retracted from the pipe, and the clamp 100 is left with its jaw carriages 30 retracted and ready for the next installation. Retraction of the jaw carriages 30 clears the jaw pads 40 from the pipe before the frame halves are swung apart.
36	
37	The latch and the force-limiting drive train
38	
39	The latch 16 comprises a latch housing 58 at the latch end, a latch handle 50, and a force-limiting spring stack 54 in a drive train between the latch handle 50 and the wedge 52, the wedge 52 being movable by the latch 16. The following description of embodiments refers to the accompanying drawings. The same reference numeral denotes the same part throughout. Terms of direction are used with respect to the frame of the clamp: the axis of the frame is the axis about which the frame is annular in the closed condition, "inward" and "radially inward" mean toward that axis, "outward" and "radially outward" mean away from it, and "circumferential" means about that axis. These terms describe relationships within the clamp and do not require the clamp to be used in any particular attitude.

Overall arrangement

FIG. 1 shows a split pipe clamp 100 closed around a pipe 90, with the latch 16 in the over-center position described below and the jaw pads 40 seated on the pipe 90. The clamp 100 has a first frame half 10 and a second frame half 12. Each of the first frame half 10 and the second frame half 12 is semicircular, and the two frame halves together surround the pipe 90. The first frame half 10 and the second frame half 12 are joined at one end, referred to as the hinge end, by a hinge 14, and are releasably joined at the other end, referred to as the latch end, by a releasable latch 16. The hinge 14 permits the first frame half 10 and the second frame half 12 to be swung apart far enough for the frame halves to be placed around the pipe 90 from the side. When the frame halves are brought together and the latch 16 is engaged, the first frame half 10 and the second frame half 12 define a frame that is annular about the axis of the frame.

Three jaw carriages 30 are distributed around the frame in the closed condition, so that the three jaw carriages 30 approach the pipe 90 from three different directions. Each jaw carriage 30 moves radially with respect to the frame and carries at its inner end a jaw pad 40, which is described below in connection with FIG. 3. The jaw pads 40 carried at the inner ends of the three jaw carriages 30 bear on the pipe 90 when the clamp 100 is clamped. The clamp 100 does not require a part dimensioned to a particular pipe diameter, and the same clamp 100 serves pipes of different diameters within the radial travel of the jaw carriages 30.

The frame may carry a mounting boss 70 outside the annular guide 18 described below, as shown in FIG. 5, which is a fragmentary view with parts shown in section on a plane containing the axis of the frame and corresponding in orientation to the plane of FIG. 3, that plane passing through the mounting boss 70. The mounting boss 70 supports equipment 80 that is to be held on the pipe 90 by the clamp 100. FIG. 5 shows the equipment 80 supported on the mounting boss 70, the equipment 80 being a sensor, a tool, or a conduit. The mounting boss 70 does not participate in the advance of the three jaw carriages 30 inwardly in synchronism. FIG. 5 also shows the annular guide 18 of the frame with the segmented cam ring 20 received in it, the mounting boss 70 standing outside the annular guide 18, no part of the mounting boss 70 reaching into the annular guide 18. The equipment 80 carried at the mounting boss 70 therefore lies outside the drive path by which the jaws are advanced. The mounting boss 70 is an optional feature of the clamp 100 and may be omitted.

The segmented cam ring

FIG. 2 shows the segmented cam ring 20, drawn removed from the frame, its segments being in the relative positions they occupy when coupled in the closed condition. The segmented cam ring 20 comprises a first cam ring segment 22 and a second cam ring segment 24. The first cam ring segment 22 is carried by the first frame half 10 and the second cam ring segment 24 is carried by the second frame half 12, so that each frame half carries one segment of the ring and each segment travels with its own frame half when the clamp 100 is opened.

The first cam ring segment 22 and the second cam ring segment 24 meet at two places, one at the hinge end and one at the latch end. At the hinge end the two segments have complementary coupling faces 26, and at the latch end they have complementary coupling faces 28. The complementary coupling faces 26 and the complementary coupling faces 28 are each shaped so that one segment can transmit circumferential force to the other through the joint. The faces are brought into engagement by the same motion that closes the frame halves: as the first frame half 10 and the second frame half 12 are swung together about the hinge 14, the complementary coupling faces 26 close on one another at the hinge end and the complementary coupling faces 28 close on one another at the latch end. FIG. 6 shows the joint at the latch end in the closed condition, the end of the first cam ring segment 22 held by the first frame half 10 and the end of the second cam ring segment 24 held by the second frame half 12, the two ends meeting at the complementary coupling faces 28.

Coupling the segments in this way solves a problem created by splitting the clamp. Here the division of the ring is undone by the act of closing the clamp. In the closed condition the first cam ring segment 22 and the second cam ring segment 24 are coupled at both ends and rotate together in the annular guide as a coupled ring, and a circumferential input applied to either segment is carried around the whole ring. One input, applied at one point on one frame half, therefore reaches every jaw carriage 30 through a single kinematic element, and the relationship between the jaw carriages 30 is set by the geometry of the ring rather than by the way the clamp is operated. When the latch 16 is released and the frame halves are swung apart, the complementary coupling faces 26 and the complementary coupling faces 28 separate and each segment stays with its own frame half, so that the coupling is made and broken by the closing and opening of the frame halves.

The annular guide 18 retains the first cam ring segment 22 on the first frame half 10 and the second cam ring segment 24 on the second frame half 12, and permits circumferential movement of the coupled ring. Each segment is therefore held on its own frame half whether the clamp 100 is open or closed, and no separate operation is needed to place the ring in the frame when the frame halves are brought together.

The segmented cam ring 20 has three oblique slots 34, one for each jaw carriage 30. Each oblique slot 34 is inclined to the radial direction of the frame at the circumferential position of that slot, so that rotation of the coupled ring produces inward travel of its jaw carriage 30, the three oblique slots 34 being arranged so that the three jaw carriages 30 travel inwardly in synchronism.

The segmented cam ring 20 further has a ring drive face 36, shown in FIG. 2 at the latch end of the ring, against which the latch 16 acts through a wedge 52 as described below. The ring drive face 36 is presented at a position on the ring that the wedge 52 can reach, so that advance of the wedge 52 against the ring drive face 36 moves the segmented cam ring 20 circumferentially.

The jaw carriages

FIG. 3 is a fragmentary sectional view through one jaw carriage 30, taken on line 3-3 of FIG. 1. The frame is formed with the annular guide 18, which receives the segmented cam ring 20 and holds it against radial movement while leaving it free to move circumferentially.

The frame is further formed with a radial guide 38 at the position of each jaw carriage 30, so that the frame in the closed condition has the annular guide 18 and three radial guides 38. Each jaw carriage 30 is received in a respective one of the three radial guides 38 and is constrained by the radial guide 38 to move radially with respect to the frame. Each jaw carriage 30 carries a follower 32 that projects from the jaw carriage 30 into a respective one of the oblique slots 34 of the segmented cam ring 20. The follower 32 bears against the sides of the oblique slot 34.

The follower 32 is constrained in two ways at once. The radial guide 38 prevents the jaw carriage 30, and therefore the follower 32, from moving circumferentially, while the oblique slot 34 holds the follower 32 at a position along the slot, which is inclined to the radial direction, so that circumferential movement of the segmented cam ring 20 displaces the follower 32 radially. When the coupled ring turns through its stroke, the side of each oblique slot 34 bears on the corresponding follower 32 and drives it, and with it the jaw carriage 30, radially inward along the radial guide 38. Because all three followers 32 are engaged in oblique slots 34 of one coupled ring, the three jaw carriages 30 advance inwardly in synchronism for as long as the ring turns. The jaw pads 40 therefore close on the pipe together.

At its inner end each jaw carriage 30 carries a jaw pad 40. The jaw pad 40 is pivotally mounted on the jaw carriage 30 and has a concave bearing face directed inwardly of the frame. Because the jaw pad 40 is free to pivot on the jaw carriage 30, the concave bearing face aligns itself with the outer surface of the pipe as it lands. The same concave bearing face therefore seats on pipes of different diameters, and no part dimensioned to a particular pipe diameter is required.

A carriage return spring 44 acts on each jaw carriage 30 so as to urge that jaw carriage 30 radially outward. When the latch 16 is released and the drive from the latch to the ring drive face 36 is removed, the carriage return springs 44 push the jaw carriages 30 outward and the jaw pads 40 are retracted from the pipe, and the clamp 100 is left with its jaw carriages 30 retracted and ready for the next installation. Retraction of the jaw carriages 30 clears the jaw pads 40 from the pipe before the frame halves are swung apart.

The latch and the force-limiting drive train

The latch 16 comprises a latch housing 58 at the latch end, a latch handle 50, and a force-limiting spring stack 54 in a drive train between the latch handle 50 and the wedge 52, the wedge 52 being movable by the latch 16. The latch housing 58 presents a fixed edge referred to below in connection with the indicator pin 56. The wedge 52 is positioned to bear on the ring drive face 36 of the segmented cam ring 20.

FIG. 4 is an enlarged fragmentary view of the latch end, with parts shown in section, and shows the latch housing 58, the latch handle 50, the wedge 52, the force-limiting spring stack 54 and the indicator pin 56 in their relation to the first cam ring segment 22, the second cam ring segment 24 and the ring drive face 36.

The latch 16 has two engaged positions. In a first position, the latch 16 holds the first frame half 10 and the second frame half 12 closed around the pipe 90 but does not clamp it: the frame is captive on the pipe 90 and cannot fall away, while the segmented cam ring 20 has not yet advanced the jaw carriages 30. In a second, over-center position, the wedge 52 drives the segmented cam ring 20 and the pipe 90 is clamped. Movement of the latch handle 50 from the first position to the second position advances the wedge 52 against the ring drive face 36. That advance moves the segmented cam ring 20 circumferentially, and the coupled ring turns through its limited stroke.

The force-limiting spring stack 54 answers the problem of what becomes of the operator's remaining handle travel. The jaw pads 40 land on the pipe 90 at some point in the stroke that depends on the diameter of the pipe 90, and the latch handle 50 has still to be carried into its over-center position. If the drive train from the latch handle 50 to the wedge 52 were rigid, that remaining travel would be taken up by whatever part of the assembly yielded first, in practice by driving one jaw farther into the pipe 90 than the others and loading it far more heavily. Additional travel of the latch handle 50 after all three jaw pads 40 have contacted the pipe 90 compresses the force-limiting spring stack 54 rather than forcing one jaw carriage 30 farther inward than the others.

The indicator pin 56 is coupled to the force-limiting spring stack 54 and projects from the latch housing 58. As the force-limiting spring stack 54 compresses, the indicator pin 56 moves relative to a fixed edge of the latch housing 58, and the position of the indicator pin 56 with respect to that fixed edge shows the operator when the force-limiting spring stack 54 has entered a predetermined compression range. The indicator pin 56 therefore reports clamp loading mechanically, and what it reports is the state of the force-limiting spring stack 54. The indicator pin 56 is displaced by compression of the force-limiting spring stack 54 independently of a diameter of the pipe 90, and its position is not a measurement of that diameter.

Operation

To install the clamp 100 on a pipe 90, the operator opens the latch 16 and swings the first frame half 10 and the second frame half 12 apart about the hinge 14. The first cam ring segment 22 stays with the first frame half 10 and the second cam ring segment 24 stays with the second frame half 12, and the complementary coupling faces 26 and the complementary coupling faces 28 are separated. The operator places the frame halves around the pipe 90 from the side and closes them about the hinge 14. Closing the frame halves brings the complementary coupling faces 26 into engagement at the hinge end and the complementary coupling faces 28 into engagement at the latch end, coupling the first cam ring segment 22 and the second cam ring segment 24 into the coupled ring within the annular guide 18.

The operator then moves the latch 16 to its first position, in which the frame is held around the pipe 90 without clamping. The operator moves the latch handle 50 to the second, over-center position. The wedge 52 is driven against the ring drive face 36, the coupled ring turns through its stroke, the sides of the three oblique slots 34 drive the three followers 32, and the three jaw carriages 30 advance inwardly in synchronism until the pivoting jaw pads 40 seat on the pipe 90. The remaining travel of the latch handle 50 compresses the force-limiting spring stack 54, and the operator watches the indicator pin 56 move relative to the fixed edge of the latch housing 58 and so sees that the force-limiting spring stack 54 has entered the predetermined compression range. The latch 16 is left in the over-center position and the clamp 100 is loaded on the pipe 90.

To remove the clamp 100, the operator releases the latch 16. The latch handle 50 comes back over center, the wedge 52 retreats from the ring drive face 36, and the force-limiting spring stack 54 is unloaded. The carriage return springs 44 then push the jaw carriages 30 radially outward, so that the jaw pads 40 lift from the pipe 90. Only then are the first frame half 10 and the second frame half 12 swung apart about the hinge 14 and the clamp 100 taken off the pipe 90. The clamp 100 may be installed again on the same pipe or on a pipe of a different diameter within the radial travel of the jaw carriages 30.

Features described above in connection with one embodiment may be combined with features described in connection with another, except where the context makes the combination impossible. The embodiments described are illustrative of the disclosed clamp and are not exhaustive of it, and the scope of protection is defined by the claims that follow rather than by any particular embodiment described here.

Ledger result: the application text (title, cross-reference, government support, field, background, summary, drawing description, detailed description, claims, abstract, numerals) traces cleanly to the inventor's disclosure, which is reproduced verbatim as the single USER passage in the conversation. Every claim limitation in claims 1-15 maps to an affirmative source sentence: split frame halves on a hinge and releasable latch; three radial jaw carriages in radial guides with pivoting concave jaw pads and no part dimensioned to a particular pipe diameter; a segmented cam ring in an annular guide with one segment per half; complementary coupling faces at the hinge and latch ends that couple on closing so the segments move as one ring; a follower per carriage in a respective oblique slot; a wedge driven by the latch against a ring drive face rotating the coupled ring through a limited stroke; outward carriage springs; the two latch positions including the over-center position; the force-limiting spring stack between handle and wedge absorbing remaining travel; the indicator pin read against a fixed edge of the latch housing over a predetermined compression range and expressly not a diameter measurement; the optional mounting boss outside the annular guide carrying a sensor, tool or conduit and not participating in synchronization; and the install/remove method. The apparatus, assembly and method claim sets are all disclosure-supported statutory classes with no means-plus-function language. Numerals are one-to-one with parts, all 26 numerals in numerals.md are used in the description, every figure's numeral list matches what the detailed description says that figure shows, the single section line is designated "3-3" consistently in FIG-1.md, FIG-3.md, 07-drawings.md and 08-detailed-description.md, and no drafting note, placeholder, open question or unresolved alternative remains anywhere in the draft. The application text also stays free of shape-justifying language: no "by way of example", "any closed outline" or similar broadening appears in the description or Brief Description, and the description's own account of the ring drive face ("presented at a position on the ring that the wedge 52 can reach") is deliberately position-neutral.

The problems are confined to the figure briefs, and all of them are functional-surface geometry that the briefs verbalize but the inventor never disclosed. Two are critical. First, FIG-2.md fixes the handedness of the cam slots and names the resulting rotation sense: the inner end of each slot is said to lie clockwise of the outer end so that "counter-clockwise rotation of the ring produced by advance of the wedge in FIG. 4" drives the followers inward. The source discloses only that the slots are oblique and that ring rotation produces synchronized inward travel; the runout direction of a cam slot and the rotational sense that clamps are substantive even under a schematic label. Second, FIG-4.md fixes the circumferential direction of the wedge drive relative to the frame parting line ("driving that band to the right, away from the parting line"). The source says only that the wedge is driven against a drive face and rotates the coupled ring through a limited stroke.

A third finding is the placement of the ring drive face 36. Both FIG-2.md and FIG-4.md put it on the first cam ring segment at that segment's latch end, "on the upper side of the right joint" and "in its face adjacent the parting line". The disclosure never says which segment carries the drive face or where along the segment it sits, and the circumferential end position of a functional drive face is substantive.

Those three choices also create a verified internal inconsistency, reported as a fourth finding. Placing the drive face on the latch-end face of segment 22 and driving that segment away from the parting line means the wedge works by separating the very latch-end complementary coupling faces 28. FIG-6.md, which depicts the latch-end joint of the clamped FIG. 1, shows those end faces lying against one another and transmitting circumferential force, and 08-detailed-description.md states that in the closed condition the segments "are coupled at both ends". The drawn drive architecture and the source-supported coupling statement cannot both hold in the clamped state.

A fifth, minor finding covers FIG-3.md and FIG-5.md, which verbalize which end of the annular guide groove is closed and which open, and route the follower axially through that groove mouth. The disclosure states only that the cam ring is "retained in an annular guide of the frame" and that each carriage "has a follower received in a respective oblique slot"; the assembly topology of a functional guide groove is not something the source supplies. All five fixes are text-level edits to figure briefs only; none requires any change to the claims, description, drawing description, numerals or abstract, and none adds a speculative embodiment to the application text.

Scope note: I did not assess patentability, novelty, validity or freedom to operate, and I did not inspect any rendered image. Background prior-art characterizations were not traced to the disclosure, as instructed; they remain for the later prior_art/ review.

findings.title: FIG. 2 brief fixes the cam-slot runout direction and names the ring rotation sense; neither is disclosed
findings.where: figures/FIG-2.md, paragraph beginning "Three elongated openings are formed in the annulus"
findings.detail: The brief specifies the handedness of the three oblique slots (which radial end of each slot lies clockwise of the other) and then names the resulting sense of ring rotation as counter-clockwise. For a cam slot this is precisely the runout direction and the radial/circumferential end positions of a functional working surface, and it is substantive even though the brief's header calls "the positions and tilt of the three slots" schematic. The inventor disclosed only that the slots are oblique and that rotation of the ring is translated into synchronized inward travel; no rotational sense, and no handedness, appears anywhere in the disclosure or conversation. The claims and description are correctly direction-neutral (claim 1: "each oblique slot being inclined to a radial direction of the frame such that rotation of the coupled ring through a stroke advances the three jaw carriages inwardly in synchronism"), so the assertion exists only in the brief and should be removed there.
findings.evidence: Candidate (figures/FIG-2.md): "The three are alike and all tilt the same way, the end of each slot nearer the inner boundary lying clockwise, as seen in this view, of the end nearer the outer boundary, so that the counter-clockwise rotation of the ring produced by advance of the wedge in FIG. 4 moves all three followers inwardly." Nearest source passage (input/disclosure.md, and identically the sole USER message in input/conversation.md): "Each jaw carriage has a follower received in a respective oblique slot of the cam ring. Closing the latch drives a wedge against a drive face of the cam ring and rotates the coupled ring through a limited stroke. The oblique slots translate that rotation into synchronized inward travel of all three jaw carriages." No affirmative passage states which end of a slot lies clockwise of the other, or in which sense the ring turns.
findings.fix: In figures/FIG-2.md, replace the quoted sentence with: "The three are alike and all tilt the same way, so that turning of the ring in one sense moves all three followers inwardly; the handedness of the tilt, and the corresponding sense of ring rotation, are not specified and are shown schematically." Make no change to the claims, the description or 07-drawings.md.

findings.title: FIG. 4 brief fixes the circumferential direction in which the wedge drives the cam ring relative to the parting line
findings.where: figures/FIG-4.md, paragraph beginning "Above the parting line a hatched enclosure, the latch housing 58"
findings.detail: The brief states the direction of the wedge's drive with respect to the frame parting line at the latch joint. Which way a wedge drives a coupled ring at a joint is contact topology and drive-path substance, not a matter of visible outline, and the schematic label at the head of the brief covers only "the extent of its contact with the wedge 52", not the direction of drive. The disclosure says only that closing the latch drives the wedge against a drive face and rotates the coupled ring through a limited stroke; it never says the driven segment moves away from (or toward) the joint. The description text is correctly neutral on this point, so the assertion is unsupported figure-only matter.
findings.evidence: Candidate (figures/FIG-4.md): "A block, the wedge 52, lies in that cavity and bears on the ring drive face 36, its advance driving that band to the right, away from the parting line, so that the coupled ring is moved circumferentially in the direction that advances the jaw carriages inwardly." Nearest source passage (input/disclosure.md): "Closing the latch drives a wedge against a drive face of the cam ring and rotates the coupled ring through a limited stroke." Compare the neutral candidate description at draft/08-detailed-description.md: "That advance moves the segmented cam ring 20 circumferentially, and the coupled ring turns through its limited stroke." No source passage gives a direction relative to the parting line.
findings.fix: In figures/FIG-4.md, replace "its advance driving that band to the right, away from the parting line, so that the coupled ring is moved circumferentially in the direction that advances the jaw carriages inwardly" with "its advance bearing on the ring drive face 36 so as to move the coupled ring circumferentially in the sense that advances the jaw carriages inwardly, the direction of that movement in this view being unspecified and shown schematically."

findings.title: Ring drive face 36 is assigned to a named segment and to a named circumferential end position at the latch joint
findings.where: figures/FIG-2.md (ring drive face paragraph and its numeral target) and figures/FIG-4.md (paragraph beginning "The right band, the first cam ring segment 22" and its numeral target)
findings.detail: Both briefs place the ring drive face on the first cam ring segment, at that segment's latch end, immediately at the joint between the two segments. The circumferential end position of a functional drive face is substantive geometry under the standard for functional faces, and the disclosure does not say which of the two segments carries the drive face, nor where along the segment it lies. The description text stays supportable by saying only that the face is "at the latch end of the ring" and "presented at a position on the ring that the wedge 52 can reach"; the segment attribution and the "upper side of the right joint" / "adjacent the parting line" positioning appear only in the briefs and should be withdrawn there.
findings.evidence: Candidate (figures/FIG-2.md): "The ring drive face 36 is a short plain face carried by the first cam ring segment 22 at its latch end, on the upper side of the right joint". Candidate (figures/FIG-4.md): "The right band, the first cam ring segment 22, presents the ring drive face 36 in its face adjacent the parting line, a short plain face". Nearest source passage (input/disclosure.md): "Closing the latch drives a wedge against a drive face of the cam ring and rotates the coupled ring through a limited stroke." The disclosure names no carrying segment and no position relative to the segment ends or the joint.
findings.fix: In figures/FIG-2.md, replace the quoted clause with: "The ring drive face 36 is a short plain face presented by the segmented cam ring 20 at the latch end of the ring, where the wedge reaches it; its position along the ring, form, extent and depth are not specified and are shown schematically." Change the FIG-2 numeral target to: "36 ring drive face: target the short plain face on the segmented cam ring 20 at the latch end where the wedge acts." In figures/FIG-4.md, replace the quoted sentence with: "One band presents the ring drive face 36, a short plain face where the wedge 52 meets it; the band that carries it, its position along that band, and its form and extent are not specified and are shown schematically." Change the FIG-4 numeral target to: "36 ring drive face: target the short plain face on the band where the wedge 52 meets it."

findings.title: Drawn drive architecture separates the latch-end coupling faces that FIG. 6 and the description show coupled in the clamped state
findings.where: figures/FIG-4.md vs. figures/FIG-6.md and draft/08-detailed-description.md, paragraph beginning "Coupling the segments in this way"
findings.detail: FIG-4.md places the ring drive face on the latch-end face of the first cam ring segment and has the wedge drive that segment away from the parting line. Taken together, the wedge works by pushing the first segment's latch-end face off the second segment's latch-end face, so during the clamping stroke the latch-end complementary coupling faces 28 cannot be in load-transmitting contact. FIG-6.md, which by 07-drawings.md and the description depicts the latch-end joint of the clamped clamp of FIG. 1, shows those same end faces lying against one another so that one segment transmits circumferential force to the other, and the description states that in the closed condition the segments are coupled at both ends. The two accounts of the clamped state are inconsistent, and the description's version is the one traceable to the disclosure.
findings.evidence: figures/FIG-4.md: "its advance driving that band to the right, away from the parting line"; figures/FIG-6.md: "At the parting line the end faces of the first cam ring segment 22 and the second cam ring segment 24 lie against one another where they meet, so that one segment can transmit circumferential force to the other"; draft/08-detailed-description.md: "In the closed condition the first cam ring segment 22 and the second cam ring segment 24 are coupled at both ends and rotate together in the annular guide as a coupled ring"; draft/07-drawings.md: "FIG. 6 is an enlarged fragmentary detail of the latch-end joint of the clamp of FIG. 1 ... with the frame halves closed." Source (input/disclosure.md): "When the halves close, complementary drive faces at the hinge and latch ends couple the segments so that they move as one ring."
findings.fix: Apply the fixes to figures/FIG-4.md and figures/FIG-2.md given in the two findings above; with the drive direction and the drive-face position no longer asserted, nothing in the brief set contradicts the coupled-at-both-ends condition shown in FIG-6.md and stated in the description. Make no change to figures/FIG-6.md, the claims or the description.

findings.title: FIG. 3 and FIG. 5 briefs state which end of the annular guide groove is closed and route the follower axially through that mouth
findings.where: figures/FIG-3.md (groove paragraph and follower paragraph) and figures/FIG-5.md (groove paragraph)
findings.detail: The briefs verbalize the opening topology of the annular guide, a functional guide groove: which end is closed, which side is open, and that the follower leaves the jaw carriage axially and passes through that mouth into the slot. Which end of a functional guide is closed, and the path by which a follower reaches its slot, are connection-and-topology statements rather than mere visible outline, so the schematic labels at the heads of the briefs do not carry them. The disclosure states only that the cam ring is retained in an annular guide and that each carriage has a follower received in a respective oblique slot; it says nothing about the axial side on which the guide opens or the direction in which the follower projects. The claims and description are correctly silent, so the correction is confined to the briefs.
findings.evidence: Candidate (figures/FIG-3.md): "The groove is bounded by the body above and below, closed at its right and open toward the left; its proportions shown schematically. That groove is the annular guide 18." and "A post extends to the right from its upper end, through the groove mouth and into that opening". Candidate (figures/FIG-5.md): "A groove is formed in it, its proportions and the direction in which it opens shown schematically, bounded by the body on its radially outer side above and its radially inner side below, closed at its right and opening toward the left of the view." Nearest source passages (input/disclosure.md): "A segmented cam ring is retained in an annular guide of the frame." and "Each jaw carriage has a follower received in a respective oblique slot of the cam ring." Neither states an opening side, a closed end, or a direction of follower projection.
findings.fix: In figures/FIG-3.md, replace "closed at its right and open toward the left; its proportions shown schematically" with "open on one side so that the follower 32 can reach the block in it, the side on which it opens and its proportions being unspecified and shown schematically", and replace "A post extends to the right from its upper end, through the groove mouth and into that opening" with "A post extends from the jaw carriage 30 through the mouth of the groove and into that opening, the position from which it projects and its direction of projection being unspecified and shown schematically". In figures/FIG-5.md, replace "closed at its right and opening toward the left of the view" with "open on one side, the side on which it opens being unspecified and shown schematically".
